newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Lebed says Moscow will not stop NATO enlargement.
newsitem.headline: Lebed says Moscow will not stop NATO enlargement.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed said on Monday that Russia would not try to stand in the way of NATO's planned eastwards expansion.
"It is NATO's business what NATO decides. Whatever NATO decides, Russia is not going to go into hysterics," he told a news conference after talks with NATO's 16 ambassadors.
Lebed, a former general and now President Boris Yeltsin's security adviser, said the problem was one of timing.
"The main thing is not to hurry, or you may trip up," Lebed said.
It was the clearest signal yet that Moscow now considered NATO expansion to include countries such as Poland, Hungary and the Czech republic as inevitable.
Russia has tried to link enlargement with a new treaty or charter governing all relations between the two former Cold War foes. NATO rejects any linkage, saying the two issues can run in parallel.
Lebed said he still favoured the "sequential approach" to prevent any misunderstandings and ensure the START 1 and START 2 arms control agreements between Russia and the West were unaffected.
But for the first time, a senior Russian official accepted NATO's argument that it was an independent organisation which had the right to do what it wished.
"Politically and legally, any legitimate organisation can join what and with who it wants to," Lebed said.
